title: ETFs, index funds, FoFs, and MF vs PMS vs AIF
objectives: Explain how an ETF, an index fund and a fund of funds differ.
Say how mutual funds, PMS and AIFs compare.
Know when a client needs a demat account.
body_md:
## Passive and fund-of-funds products

| Product | How it works | How to buy | Watch for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Index fund | Copies an index such as the Nifty 50; no stock-picking | From the AMC at NAV | Tracking error; the TER |
| ETF | Index-linked units traded on the stock exchange | Through a demat and trading account at market price | The gap between market price and NAV; liquidity |
| Fund of funds (FoF) | Invests in other funds' units, not directly in securities | From the AMC at NAV | Two layers of cost; tax follows the underlying fund type |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: tax treatment of FoFs and the debt-fund rules change with the Finance Act. -->

## MF, PMS and AIF side by side

| | Mutual fund | PMS | AIF |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum ticket | As low as a few hundred rupees | ₹50 lakh | Typically ₹1 crore |
| Ownership | Units of a pooled fund | Securities in the client's own demat | Units of a pooled fund |
| Customisation | None | Some, such as stock exclusions | None |
| Taxation | At fund level; investor taxed on redemption | Every trade is taxed in the client's hands | Depends on the category |
| Transparency | Monthly portfolio disclosure | Full view of every holding and trade | Periodic reporting |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: ticket sizes and fee limits per the current SEBI PMS and AIF regulations. -->

Higher minimums do not mean better returns. They mean a different structure, different costs and more concentrated risk. Module 2 covers PMS in depth.

> **Investor takeaway:** Pick the structure that fits your goal and size, not the one that sounds exclusive.
example: A client with ₹5 lakh wants 'something like the Nifty with low cost'. An index fund is bought from the AMC at NAV and needs no demat. An ETF on the same index needs a demat and trading account, and is bought at a market price that may differ slightly from NAV.
say: An ETF trades on the exchange like a share. An index fund is bought from the fund house at NAV.
PMS and AIF need much larger amounts and have different risks. Let's see if they fit later.
never: PMS always beats a mutual fund.
An ETF and an index fund work exactly the same way.

check.q: Which product needs a demat and trading account to buy?
check.why: ETFs trade on the stock exchange, so a demat and trading account is needed.

check.q: What does a fund of funds invest in?
check.why: A fund of funds invests in other funds' units.

check.q: What is the minimum ticket for a PMS?
check.why: A PMS requires a minimum of ₹50 lakh. AIFs typically need ₹1 crore.
